Optics Express · First author

Attention-assisted signal recovery for photonic ADCs

A power- and sampling-rate-agnostic learning pipeline for nonlinear equalization and denoising in a time-stretched photonic analog-to-digital converter.

At a glance

Recover high-fidelity signals without retraining at every operating point.

Photonic ADCDeep learningCalibrationDenoising
Problem & physical context

Photonic time-stretch ADCs extend capture bandwidth, but the real signal chain adds nonlinear distortion through electro-optic modulation, filtering, dispersion, photodetection, and electronic digitization. A correction model tied to one input power or sampling rate is difficult to deploy.

Method

The two-stage architecture separates nonlinear equalization from denoising. Training data pair known references with signals passed through the physical front end, encouraging the representation to learn system distortion rather than memorize one acquisition setting.

Results & significance

The reported system reached 63 dB SNDR and 10.18 effective bits with a 1 GSa/s electronic ADC, while reducing required electronic ADC bandwidth by three times. The architecture was evaluated across RF inputs from 0.6 to 1.4 GHz and across changing input power.

The work was selected among the top undergraduate projects at IIT Madras’s Electrical Engineering Research Scholars’ Symposium.

Contribution

As first author, Medha worked across system modelling, data generation, learning architecture, evaluation, and paper preparation, in collaboration with Mandeep Singh and faculty mentors Prof. Deepa Venkitesh and Prof. Lakshmi Narasimhan Theagarajan.
